free_text: The patient is a 64-year-old male with an elevated PSA of 7.3 and a cT1c prostate cancer, characterized by a Gleason score of 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2). An mpMRI revealed a PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone. The management assessment is to review individual treatment benefit and preferences. The trade-off involves balancing the risk of progression with the potential benefits of treatment given the established pathological findings.
